extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for TV news producers on selecting which stories run in a newscast, ordering them in a rundown, choosing formats, and making live adjustments to maximize audience and production practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency, breaking developments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to recent events or breaking developments; fresher events have higher news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Local relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories closer to the audience (geographically or culturally) get higher priority for TV newscasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable people involved
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involvement of public figures, officials, or celebrities increases a story's newsworthiness and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Number affected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How many people are affected or could be affected by the event; larger impact raises importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension, dispute
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of conflict, dispute, or controversy makes a story more compelling and often more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual, surprising
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual or surprising elements increase viewer interest and news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals / Visual Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong video available (TV-distinctive); visual potential is a primary differentiator from print
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TV, availability of compelling visuals is a major factor: live capability, action footage, aerials, eyewitness video, and any promotable visuals boost a story's priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rundown document elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronological list of every newscast element
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include story slug; format (package, anchor read, live shot, interview, VO, VOSOT); duration; anchor/reporter assignment; graphics/video associated; tease/promo placement. Use this to plan timing and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead story selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead story = highest news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the single highest-news-value item as the lead to open the show and capture audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group related topics (clustering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group like topics (crime cluster, health cluster)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cluster similar stories for narrative coherence, but be mindful of pacing and variety so clusters don't bore viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long single-topic stretches
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 5+ minutes of one topic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't run more than about five minutes of continuous coverage on a single topic to maintain audience interest and show flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block structuring (A/B/C blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A-block = top stories; B-block = developing/lower-priority; C-block = lighter/kicker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the show into blocks: A-block for hardest news, B-block for important but lower-priority/developing items, and C-block for lighter fare or the show kicker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard–soft alternation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate hard and soft stories to retain audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix heavier, serious stories with lighter pieces to maintain pace and viewer retention throughout the newscast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format selection (package, VOSOT, VO, anchor read, live shot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format decisions affect newsworthiness and presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose formats by story needs: package (~1:30) for top stories with full reporter narration; VOSOT (~30s with anchor + soundbite) for supplemental pieces; VO (~20s) for light coverage; anchor read when visuals are minimal; live shots for ongoing/developing stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time flexibility / breaking news readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer ready to scrap rundown for breaking news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to overhaul the rundown for breaking developments; finalize newscast typically 1–2 hours before air and keep 'float' stories ready to fill gaps if the A-block is thin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live shot capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the story be presented as a live shot or live report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live capability increases a story's news value because it signals immediacy and can be more engaging for viewers; consider logistics and crew availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling/actionable video availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling video — fire, crash, protest; action footage vs. static shots
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories with dynamic, action-oriented footage are stronger for TV; static shots (e.g., empty buildings) are weaker unless paired with other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsmaker on camera / interviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsmaker on camera — interview, quote; newmaker availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to put a newsmaker on camera (or get a soundbite) enhances credibility and viewer interest; availability of sources affects placement and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial / drone potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Aerial / drone — large-scale events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aerial footage can provide scale and spectacle (e.g., large events, disasters) and increase a story's visual appeal and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyewitness footage / authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Eyewitness footage — authenticity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-person or eyewitness video lends immediacy and authenticity; verify provenance and legal/ethical considerations before airing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tease-ability / promotability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tease-ability — promotable visual
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that can be teased/promoted well (strong visuals or surprising elements) are useful for attracting and retaining viewers across the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio quality / soundbite-worthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio quality — interviewable, soundbite-worthy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good audio/soundbites make short-form TV elements effective; poor audio can limit format choices and reduce a story's usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Length-appropriateness — fits 30s–1:30 windows
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story can be told well within standard TV windows; overly complex stories may not fit short formats, affecting placement or format choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsmaker availability / logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Can we get an interview? production feasibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical considerations—can reporters reach the scene, can talent and crew be assigned, and can interviews be secured—shape whether a story is practical to run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pace and variety contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Pace/variety contribution — fits flow of show
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how a story affects the show's overall pacing and variety; choose items that contribute to a balanced, engaging newscast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics-friendly potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphics-friendly — can we make a chart?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that lend themselves to informative graphics or charts enhance viewer comprehension and can strengthen placement or format.
